Overall, throughout the analytical modeling module I learned quite a bit. For starters, I had never used the sympy solve function before so it was really neat to see that it is so readily available to shorten arithmetic timelines if needed, I really haven't seen a ton of other options that can do that. Also, the generating data portion was really neat, I would usually just use something like np.random to generate a wide range of data within some bounds but to have it as easy as one function call essentially is incredibely convenient and cool to have as an option. Lastly, the genetic search method was really cool to use, StackGP specifically, it took me a bit due to a few syntax errors in my code but once I got it working and actually understood a lot of the working components, I was very impressed with how many different equation types the program cycles through to find the best overall fit to the data, I will most likely be using this in the future, on my very own project. This work connects to my own project in a pretty impactful way as one route I can take as to reconstruct the waveform taken from the spectrometer, so coupling some other mathematics with this could be a super useful tool for doing my project in a more condensed and efficeint manner. Overall, I will most likely be using StackGP pretty heavily throughout my tenure as a grad student and most likely professional life as it is incredibely cool that there is a tool that checks all these different equation types to find the best overall fit, it will be incredibely useful for many different areas of my research regarding the spectroscopy data and reconstructing waveforms.
